evidence_type: Eyewitness; forensic (blood matching); recovery (knife and shirt); medical (post-mortem)
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 IPC; sentence not specified in the judgment
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence upheld
neutral_facts: On the evening of the incident, the victim and the accused were walking a few steps ahead of the victim's sister-in-law, who was returning from a local market. She saw them grapple with each other and then saw the accused stab the victim several times with a knife the accused was carrying. The victim collapsed and the accused ran away. The victim was first taken to a nearby private clinic and then advised to go to a hospital, where the victim was declared dead on arrival. A post-mortem the next day recorded multiple incised stab wounds on the body. One wound entered the left chest cavity, injuring the pericardium and the tip of the left ventricle; the examining doctor opined that this injury was sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, which was due to shock and haemorrhage. The doctor stated that the injuries were possible with the recovered knife, which had been produced in a sealed parcel. An FIR was registered the same day based on the eyewitness's statement. Shortly afterwards, police received information and found the accused coming from the side of a drain, carrying a blood-stained knife and wearing a blood-stained shirt. The accused was apprehended and the knife and shirt were recovered. Forensic analysis found that the victim's blood matched blood on the knife. The eyewitness described the sequence of events in detail, having watched from a short distance, and was cross-examined at length without any material discrediting her testimony.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from multiple stab wounds; post-mortem recorded eight incised wounds, with the chest wound entering the left chest cavity and held sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of PW-2; forensic blood match between victim and knife; recovery of blood-stained knife and shirt from the accused by PW-12 shortly after the murder; post-mortem findings consistent with the weapon
witness_credibility: PW-2 (sister-in-law) treated as the star and reliable eyewitness; lengthy cross-examination did not discredit her; court accepted her account of the sequence of events
post_offence_conduct: Fled the scene after the stabbing; caught the same day in the vicinity carrying the blood-stained knife and wearing a blood-stained shirt
bail_history: Interim bail granted by order dated 09.05.2012; vacated by the Supreme Court, and the appellant directed to surrender

investigation_status: FIR registered 28.05.1993 at Police Station Kashmere Gate; chargesheet filed; 18 prosecution witnesses examined at trial
procedural_irregularity: None noted; doubts raised by the defence on the manner of recovery of the knife were held not to move the case
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC. High Court (CRLA No.130 of 1997, order dated 02.07.2010): conviction and sentence upheld. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Daylight murder established by a reliable eyewitness, supported by the blood match between the victim and the knife and the same-day recovery of the knife and shirt from the accused; the judgment does not separately record the State's oral arguments
defence_argument: Prosecution failed to establish any motive; doubts raised on the manner of recovery of the knife
legal_principle_applied: Absence of motive is of little or no consequence where a reliable eyewitness, with nothing to discredit the testimony, establishes the crime
